mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden inflation spike above 3.0% triggers investor concerns about tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as risk aversion rises.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in >70% of instances where CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0, or the 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising demand (GDPC1) coupled with falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a dual positive signal, amplifying S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days as investors anticipate both higher corporate earnings and lower financing costs.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises >5% and FEDFUNDS falls >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day returns are not significantly higher than a model using only GDPC1 or FEDFUNDS individually (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rates above 3.5% post-recession signals labor market recovery, prompting positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as investors anticipate economic stabilization.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in >60% of instances where UNRATE meets the trigger condition, or the Rank IC < 0.05 over 5-year periods.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high federal funds rates above 5.0% signal tight monetary policy, reducing growth expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) in >80% of triggered instances, or the 5-day return is not below -1%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong demand growth (GDPC1) alongside robust supply expansion (INDPRO) creates a positive feedback loop, driving S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as market optimism intensifies.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises >10 and INDPRO rises >95 over the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day returns are not significantly higher than a model using only GDPC1 or INDPRO individually (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC < 0.1 over 4-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) paired with falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market strengthening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days as investor confidence surges.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >5% and UNRATE falls >0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in >50% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC < 0.1 over 3-year periods.

mechanism_narrative: A deflationary environment marked by CPIAUCSL below 2.5% and falling FEDFUNDS rates below 4.0% creates dual positive signals, driving S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as investors anticipate sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.5 and FEDFUNDS < 4.0 over the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day returns are not significantly higher than a model using only CPIAUCSL or FEDFUNDS individually (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC < 0.1 over 5-year windows.
